page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server belonging to the g2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The server exhibits weak single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and general system operations, such as Redis SET and static web serving, perform in the average middle 50% tier. Conversely, the bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference. Specifically, prompt processing and text generation speeds for both small and medium models rank in the highest tier, demonstrating a strong contrast between modest CPU capabilities and high-efficiency GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads. By pairing a capable 24 GB VRAM accelerator with a modest 8-vCPU host configuration, it avoids the overhead of over-provisioned CPU and memory resources. This makes the server highly suitable for low-to-medium scale LLM inference, graphics rendering, and machine learning model deployment, while it is less optimal for CPU-bound compilation, heavy database operations, or workloads requiring high local storage IOPS.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance does not include local storage. Benchmark results highlight a clear tradeoff: while single-core and multi-core CPU performance metrics fall into the bottom 25%, the GPU-accelerated capabilities deliver top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for LLM inference tasks using 135M and 7B models. System memory bandwidth and database operations remain in the average tier. This resource profile makes the g2-standard-8 a cost-efficient option for machine learning inference, small-to-medium model deployment, and GPU-accelerated graphics processing, where massive CPU compute is not the primary requirement.
